narration.text: Four minutes. The same player. Two very different goals.
The 1986 World Cup quarter-final. Argentina against England.
Diego Maradona put the first one in with his hand.
It became known as the Hand of God.
Then he dribbled past five England players and scored again.
FIFA later voted it the Goal of the Century. Every goal has a story.

Belgrade, 1976. Czechoslovakia against West Germany.
The final went to penalties.

narration.text: Goalkeepers used to pick up every back pass.

facts.claim: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992 to discourage time-wasting after the 1990 World Cup was criticised as dull, with goalkeepers holding up the ball.
facts.quote: The back-pass rule was introduced in 1992 to discourage time-wasting and unduly defensive play after the 1990 World Cup was widely criticised as excessively dull, rife with back-passing and goalkeepers holding up the ball to waste time.

facts.claim: The rule was introduced to discourage time-wasting and unduly defensive play.
